title: European tours and recordings with Milt Buckner, Jo Jones and others
summary: He toured England, Spain, Italy and Germany with Buckner and Jones, and recorded since 1972 with Big Joe Turner, Wild Bill Davis, Al Casey and others.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now, also in the -- was it in the '60s or in the '70s where you toured Europe with your own band, with Jo Jones and --
That's right, yeah.
-- Milt Buckner.
Milt Buckner, that's right, and of course, I've toured quite a few places, many places. I've been many places in England.
With that particular group?
Yes.
And you played Spain?
Yes, Spain, Italy and my goodness, Germany, quite a few places.
HEMLOCK
How did you find leading that band?

Well, we went over there more or less to make recordings and go on tour, you know, which we did make quite a few recordings. As of late, you know, as far back as 1972, I've made quite a few recordings with, like you said, Milt Buckner, Jo Jones and Big Joe Turner, the blues singer.
Oh, he worked with you all too?
Sure, yes, right. I made recordings with Wild Bill Davis. He was known as an organist, but he also played piano.
So did you do that with -- did he join the trio that you had?
Well, yes, they made up the trios over there during our tour over there, to make -- different ones would join on the recordings, you know.
Oh, for the recording certain things. But now, when you went there, had you chosen to use Buckner and Jones, as far as your band?
Yes, that's right.
And then when you got there, you made recordings with other situations.
That's right, that's right.
Okay. Yeah, because at first, it kind of sounded as though you did.
HEMLOCK ERASABLE
Al?
Al Casey on guitar. Do you remember
Yeah.
Joe Marshall on drums, you know, and of course, I mentioned before, Johnny Guarnieri on piano, Jimmy Shirley on guitar and Jackie Williams on drums.
So those were the groups that you recorded with when you were there.
Oh, sure, yes.
